six_added_reference_contexts.reference: Avula NVS, Veesam SK, Behera S, Balasubramanian S. Building robust machine learning models for small chemical science data: the case of shear viscosity of fluids. Machine Learning: Science and Technology. 2022;3:045032. https://doi.org/10.1088/2632-2153/acac01.
citation_contexts: Small-data viscosity prediction already separates model selection, performance estimation and physical interpolation behavior [16]. Here the input is a partial flow curve and the output is a joint law over the remaining rates. Representation selection also has supervised precedents, including principal covariates regression [17]. Quadratic loss approximations and Gaussian uncertainty have clear sensitivity-based precedents [18]; they should not be confused with physical curvature of a flow curve. These connections motivate testing the chosen representation rather than presenting low-dimensional compression or Gaussian approximation as new probability theory.

findings.text: In the original comparison, curvature lowers bounded CRPS from 0.052243 to 0.048253 and Gaussian CRPS from 0.049908 to 0.043277 (Fig. 3a). The Gaussian curvature model improves on that original random Gaussian for 20/25 formulations and on the same-code bounded model for 22/25. Eight additional fixed random codes obtain macro CRPS0.049848–0.065362, all worse than the frozen curvature code, but the prior-KL code is stronger at 0.037139 (Fig. S6; Table S13). The fixed 45 degree curvature rotation gives 0.043156, demonstrating a small constraint-orientation effect within the same span. These outcomes support a useful low-capacity correction and the value of testing representations; they do not establish curvature as the best examined representation or select a new deployment model.

findings.text: The eight new random macro scores range from 0.049848 to 0.065362, all above the original curvature 0.043277. Prior-KL obtains 0.037139 macro CRPS,0.098648 pooled log RMSE and 0.073284 one-sided CRPS, but its mean joint log density 63.327985 is below curvature 63.658108 and conditional Gaussian 82.925879. Overall KL wins 19/25 formulations. In the middle gap, however, it wins only 8/25 and loses 17/25; its mean difference is−0.00060448 but median difference is+0.00083818. Arithmetic removal of P0 leaves a mean difference of only−0.00002107; all official results retain P0. KL covers 11/33 P0 middle-gap targets versus 8/33 for curvature. This does not repair local reliability.

findings.text: Trace fractions divide the trace of the code-explained block by trace(V0); mean point fractions average the 33 diagonal ratios. They weight positions differently. For example, prior-KL one-sided allocation 0.988047 does not mean 98.80%accuracy, physical information recovered or physical variance explained. All 150 conditional code covariances have rank 2; no eigenmode is discarded, no jitter is added, and every residual is positive definite. The analysis states explicit machine-precision rank/support tolerances and retains all results. It cannot prove prediction quality, calibration, physical identifiability or new-batch transfer.
